text:
Samira (CS): quick thread — putting together a compact customer-facing handbook for onboarding teams that covers prefetching, small-batch tuning, and streaming fallbacks. want this to be a 1-page checklist + 3 runnable snippets customers can drop into their infra. thoughts?
Tom (FieldOps): love it. please call out jitter on prefill schedules and a conservative default for batch_size (start small). many customers hit cold-cache spikes.
Jules (SRE): agree. also include guidance for circuit breakers and graceful degradation when streaming fails. simple heuristics: 1) retry with exponential backoff, 2) fall back to synchronous non-stream generation, 3) add a max latency budget per request.
Priya (CSM): can we add a short section mapping these to renewal-risk signals? e.g., repeated timeouts in first 7 days = high risk, repeated low-quality outputs = medium risk — helps CSMs prioritize.
Samira (CS): yes — we'll include red/yellow/green triggers and a 3-step remediation playbook for each. also capture a short feedback capture form customers can send back.
OnboardBot: automated note: attach onboarding telemetry dashboard link -> https://console.redwood/integrations/onboard-telemetry (example).
Tom (FieldOps): for prefetch TTL: recommend start with 60s for conversational contexts, 300s for assistant-style profiles. add randomized jitter +-20% to prevent thundering herd.
Jules (SRE): mini code snippet for clients (python pseudocode):
```
# prefetch strategy (pseudo)
def prefetch(user_id, prompt_prefix):
  if cache.hit(user_id, prompt_prefix):
    return cache.get(user_id, prompt_prefix)
  resp = call_inference_model(prompt_prefix, max_tokens=0)  # warm KV
  cache.set(user_id, prompt_prefix, resp.kv_head, ttl=base_ttl * rand(0.8,1.2))
```

Samira (CS): include an ops-safe batching example too. small batch example: batch_size=4, max_wait=20ms, adaptive_downscale when p95 latency > target.
Tom (FieldOps): add note: batch_size should be tunable by route. e.g., short chat completions -> small batches, batch-friendly bulk embeddings -> larger batches.
Priya (CSM): for customer-facing runbook, let's have: 1) One-line summary, 2) Quick checklist (flags to flip), 3) Snippets, 4) When to call CS/SE, 5) Feedback form link. Keep language non-technical for product managers.
Samira (CS): agreed. also add a short troubleshooting table: symptom -> quick checks -> mitigation. example: "spike in 5xx" -> check region fallback, capacity tier, KV cache warm ratio -> temporary scale-up or enable fallback model.
Jules (SRE): telemetry keys to capture: cache_hit_ratio, avg_batch_size, stream_error_rate, p50/p95 latency, model_fallback_count. include sample SIEM query for each.
Tom (FieldOps): operational tip: pre-warm pools for go-live windows and use staged ramp with 10/30/60 min warm phases. include a short script example to schedule warm jobs.
Priya (CSM): I'll draft the renewal-risk escalation triggers and a one-click shareable doc we can send during 7-day check-ins.
Samira (CS): perfect. action items: Priya drafts risk mapping + feedback form by EOD Thu; Jules adds telemetry snippets and the two code blocks; Tom writes the warmup schedule and jitter notes; I'll assemble into a 1-page PDF and a customer-friendly HTML playbook.
Jules (SRE): ping if you want a sample prometheus query; I can paste a few.
Tom (FieldOps): +1. also include an example fallback policy config: region -> fallback_model -> max_latency_ms. small JSON example.
Samira (CS): thanks all. final ask: keep each snippet <=12 lines so we can inline in email. will share draft tomorrow for review. :thumbsup:
Priya (CSM): cheers, will review once ready.
OnboardBot: reminder scheduled: send follow-up checklist 3 days after go-live (automated).
